To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we provide an almost globally converging observer, and an almost globally convergening trajectory tracking controller for an aerial robot tethered to the ground by either a cable or a rigid bar.

we have designed an almost globally converging nonlinear controller that can be implemented onboard an aerial robot connected by a passive cable to the ground and that we have designed a nonlinear observer for this system that can be implemented on board an aerial robot connected either by a passive cable, or by a passive rigid bar, to the ground.
the aerial robot tethered by a cable or by a bar is a differentially flat dynamical system that is observable and controllable, and that it can be globally controlled and observed in real time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and analysis of nonlinear models for aerial robots connected to the ground via cables or bars.
the design of controllers and observers for a novel class of nonlinear robotic systems.
the development of a complete nonlinear control framework for aerial vehicles connected by passive cables or bars.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work presents the first complete nonlinear control solution for aerial robots tethered to the ground by cables or bars.
the proposed method can robustly control the system under the most severe conditions.

this paper provides a thorough and rigorous characterization of this nonlinear robotic system in terms both of its dynamical properties (flatness, controllibility, observability) and of the design of controllers, observers, and estimators for the full state of the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to design a controller and an observer for an aerial robot connected by a passive link, and the performance is satisfactory even in far from nominal conditions.

we have provided an in depth analysis of the dynamics and the control of a tethered aerial vehicle and we have proposed a novel observer and two nonlinear controllers that are robust to a variety of uncertainties and disturbances.
we have provided a complete and rigorous analysis of the dynamics and control of aerial robots connected to the ground with a cable or a rigid link.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a tethered aerial robot is a very interesting nonlinear dynamical system that can be effectively and robustly controlled and estimated.

the proposed controllers and observers are able to handle the nonlinearities, uncertainties, and disturbances of the system, and to track the reference trajectories with a high level of precision and robustness.
the dynamics of a tethered aerial robot are well understood, which allows us to design controllers and observers that are guaranteed to be almost globally convergent.
